sourcedFrom: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION (none printed)
cleanIntro: Knight's own instruction is to clean and lubricate after every day's shooting. Black powder and its approved substitutes are corrosive and deposit residue in the bore, breech plug, hammer, receiver and trigger — stainless included, which is more corrosion resistant than blued steel but is not corrosion proof.

steps.title: Prove the bore is empty
steps.action: Work through the maker's three pre-handling checks before anything else. Safeties rearward and functioning, no primer in the receiver live or spent, then stand the rifle on its butt and drop the ramrod down the bore. A ramrod tip that comes up near flush with the muzzle is the only proof that there is no charge sitting on top of the breech plug. A tip standing proud of the muzzle by an inch or more means the rifle is still loaded and must be dealt with as a loaded gun, not stripped.
steps.quote: 1.) Confirm that all safeties are functioning properly and are in the safe position. 2.) Check that there is no primer, either live or spent, installed. 3.) Place the rifle butt on the ground, remove the ramrod, and place it in the bore. If the ramrod tip is near flush with the muzzle, the rifle is unloaded and the bore free from obstruction. Remove the ramrod from the barrel.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Loading and Firing, Preparing to Load — p.11
steps.warn: A muzzleloader gives you no extractor and no ejection port. The ramrod depth check is the only unloaded check there is.

steps.title: Clear a charge without firing it
steps.action: The DISC Extreme is a bolt action with a removable breech plug, and that combination lets you push a live charge out the back rather than shooting it off. Pull the bolt, back the breech plug out, and drive the bullet and powder rearward with the ramrod into a container. Do this outdoors, away from any ignition source, and never with a primer still fitted.
steps.quote: The design also allows you to unload the rifle without firing by pushing unfired powder and/or bullet out the back of the barrel with the ramrod.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Action and Safety Systems, Bolt Action — p.34

steps.title: Confirm before you touch a solvent
steps.action: Knight puts this warning at the head of the cleaning section rather than in the strip section, and it is worth reading twice. Solvent, hot water and a bore brush all apply force down a barrel that may still hold a charge. Re-check the receiver for a primer even if you cleared the rifle ten minutes ago.
steps.quote: WARNING! Before cleaning, be certain that the rifle is unloaded and that no primer is in the receiver. Cleaning a loaded or primed rifle may result in accidental discharge.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning — p.9
steps.warn: Cleaning a loaded or primed rifle may result in accidental discharge.

steps.title: Know which action you are working on
steps.action: Read your own model's page before you start. The DISC Extreme takes a removable bolt and a removable stainless breech plug, and the plug is cut for .50 and .52 calibre — plugs are not interchangeable across the range and the wrong one will either not seat or will not carry the flame. The identification table is on printed page 22.
steps.aside: Breech plugs differ by calibre AND by model. Check the identification table on p.22 before fitting a replacement.
steps.quote: Action: Patented Double Safety System, New C-Toolless, Quick Release, Removable Bolt Assembly. Removable Stainless Steel Breech Plug (see page 22 for breech plug identification for .50 and .52 caliber).
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Knight DISC Extreme — p.30

steps.title: Check what your rifle is primed by
steps.action: Ignition decides what you will find fouled and what you must clean out. Bare-primer rifles foul the primer pocket in the bolt face and the breech plug flash channel; Full Plastic Jacket rifles carry the primer in a disposable red jacket that seals the receiver. Musket-cap rifles use a nipple-style plug instead. Know which you have before you go looking for residue.
steps.quote: Ignition: Full Plastic Jacket™, 209 Primer or #11, Musket Cap
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Knight DISC Extreme — p.30

steps.title: Set up before you break anything down
steps.action: Get a padded vise and a parts tray on the bench first. The breech plug can take real force to start, and doing that with the barrel held in bare jaws is how a barrel gets marked. The schematic letters in the steps that follow — (O), (W), (S7), (I) — are the manual's own part labels, so keep the schematic to hand.
steps.quote: It is advisable to use a padded vise to remove and reinstall the breech plug. Place small parts in a pan to avoid losing them.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly — p.35

steps.title: Ramrod out
steps.action: Draw the ramrod (O) out of the thimbles under the forend and set it aside. It has to come out before the barrelled action will lift clear of the stock, and it is the part most easily bent by leaving it in place while you wrestle the stock screw.
steps.quote: 1.) Remove the ramrod (O) from the stock and set aside.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.35

steps.title: Barrelled action out of the stock
steps.action: One stock screw holds the whole barrelled action in, just forward of the trigger guard (W). Back it out fully, then lift the barrel and receiver away from the stock rather than prising them — the recoil lug is a close fit and levering it chips the inletting. Set the stock aside where it will not get solvent on it.
steps.quote: 2.) Remove the barreled action from the stock.The barreled action is held in the stock with one stock screw. It is located just forward of the trigger guard (W). Remove this screw and care-fully separate the barrel assembly from the stock. Set the stock aside.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.35

steps.title: Trigger assembly and bolt out
steps.action: The trigger assembly comes off as a unit on one mounting screw (S7) — do not take the unit itself apart. Then lift the bolt handle, pull open the quick-release detent screw on the LEFT side of the receiver, and draw the bolt straight back and out. The detent has to be held open the whole time the bolt is passing it; releasing it early is what makes a bolt feel jammed halfway.
steps.caution: The quick-release detent screw is on the LEFT side of the receiver. Hold it open until the bolt is fully clear.
steps.quote: 3.) Remove the trigger assembly. Remove the trigger mounting screw (S7), and lift the trigger assembly from the receiver. Remove the bolt. Lift the bolt handle up, pull open the quick release detent screw that holds the bolt in place from the left side of the receiver, and pull the bolt out.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.35

steps.title: Soap and water, but read the label
steps.action: Black powder and its substitutes are corrosive, so the cleaning agent is hot soapy water or an approved solvent — but not any soap. Chlorides, lye and bleach strip bluing, and a dishwasher tablet or a household bleach cleaner will do visible damage in one session. Stainless is more corrosion resistant than blued steel and is still not corrosion proof; clean it the same way.
steps.quote: 2.) Clean rifle with soap and water or an approved solvent. Do not use soaps with chlorides, lye, or bleach in them; the chemicals may remove blueing on your barrel.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Trigger group: solvent only, never water
steps.action: This is the one absolute in Knight's cleaning section. The breech plug and the bolt or hammer go into hot soapy water; the trigger assembly does not, on any Knight rifle. Clean it with solvent, wipe it out, and put a drop of oil on the sear. And do not park any part in a solvent bath while you go and do something else — extended soaking is called out separately.
steps.quote: 3.) Clean your rifle from the breech end. Place your breech plug and hammer in hot soapy water or Knight® Solvent™. Do not use water to clean triggers on any Knight® Rifle. Only a solvent should be used to clean these Knight Rifles. Clean with appropriate material and lubricate sear. Don’t allow barreled action and other rifle parts to soak in soapy water or solvents for extended periods.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10
steps.warn: Never put a Knight trigger assembly in water. Solvent only.

steps.title: Scrub the bore from the breech end
steps.action: With the plug out you can clean the barrel the way it was designed to be cleaned — straight through, breech to muzzle, so fouling leaves the bore instead of being driven back into the breech. Stand the muzzle in the hot water, put a patch on the jag at the rear of the receiver and push it through. Repeat until a patch comes out clean, not until you are bored.
steps.quote: 4.) Use a Knight® Ultimate Range Rod™ or a ramrod with a Knight® Bullet Starter™ handle and an attached cleaning jag.With the muzzle still in the hot soapy water, place a patch over the rear of the receiver and push into the barrel. Scrub the bore vigorously to completely remove all foreign matter, powder residue, and fouling. Repeat this as many times as necessary to get a clean bore.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Detail the receiver, hammer and small parts
steps.action: A toothbrush and pipe cleaners get into the corners a patch cannot: the receiver interior, the bolt face or hammer, the plug itself, and around the trigger. Fouling left in a corner is where rust starts, and on a bare-primer rifle the primer pocket collects a hard ring of residue that needs picking out rather than wiping.
steps.quote: 6.) Using a toothbrush or pipe cleaner, thoroughly clean the receiver , hammer, breech plug, trigger and other components of all residues, fouling, etc.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Dry completely, then oil generously
steps.action: Water cleaning only works if the drying is total. Every wetted surface — bore, receiver interior, plug threads, under the barrel where it sat in the stock — gets dried and then oiled with a water-displacing rust inhibitor. This is the step people skip on the inside surfaces, and it is the inside surfaces that pit.
steps.quote: 7.) Thoroughly dry all metal surfaces and generously lubricate your rifle inside and out using Knight® Oil™ with rust inhibitor.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The DISC Extreme is now down to its owner-level groups: stock, barrelled action, trigger assembly and bolt, with the bore and receiver cleaned and oiled. From here you either reassemble in your model's own order, or go on to Deep Clean for the breech plug and the striker-level bolt strip.
steps.quote: 8.) Reassemble your muzzleloader according to the instructions in your model’s section of this manual.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

deepSteps.title: Breech plug out
deepSteps.action: Put the barrel in the padded vise. Engage the breech plug wrench end of the combo tool on the plug (I) through the rear of the receiver and turn it anticlockwise. A plug that has been fired and not greased can take serious force to start — the combo tool is drilled so you can pass a rod through it for leverage. Force applied straight, once, beats repeated snatching.
deepSteps.caution: Use a padded vise. Levering on an unsupported barrel marks it.
deepSteps.quote: 4.) Remove the breech plug. Insert the combo tool (breech plug wrench side) into the receiver, engage the breech plug (I) and turn it counterclockwise.This may require a considerable amount of force. (Holes in the combo tool allow a rod to be used for added leverage.)
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.35

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug threads in the receiver
deepSteps.action: The female threads in the receiver hold more baked-on fouling than any other surface on the rifle, and a plug torqued down onto that fouling is what seizes. A toothbrush will do the outer threads; a bullet starter with an adapter and a 20 gauge shotgun brush reaches the full depth. Do this every time the plug comes out.
deepSteps.quote: 5.) Thoroughly scrub and clean the breech plug threads in the receiver. A toothbrush, bottle brush, or bullet starter with adapter and 20 gauge shotgun brush work well for this task.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

deepSteps.title: Bolt out for cleaning
deepSteps.action: Knight gives the bolt its own sequence and tells you to follow it in order to avoid misalignment. Handle up, hold the spring-loaded quick-release bolt screw out, and draw the bolt from the receiver. Doing it in any other order is what leaves the striker and bolt body out of index later.
deepSteps.quote: 1.) With the rifle bolt handle in the up position, while pulling out on the spring loaded Quick Release bolt screw (Photo #1), pull the bolt out of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Draw the cocking piece up on the secondary safety
deepSteps.action: Turning the secondary safety clockwise pulls the cocking piece up against the front edge of the safety and takes the striker spring's load off the threads. This is the step that makes the striker unscrew by hand instead of fighting you, and skipping it is how the reference marks end up out of alignment.
deepSteps.quote: 2.) Turn the secondary safety clockwise until the cocking piece is drawn up against the front edge of secondary safety. (Photo #2)
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Striker assembly off — and stop there
deepSteps.action: Unscrew the striker assembly anticlockwise until it comes free of the bolt body. That is the end of the owner-level strip. Knight states plainly that going further is not required and may mean sending the bolt back to be reassembled, so clean the striker and the bolt body as the two units they are.
deepSteps.quote: 3.) Unscrew the striker assembly counterclockwise, until it is free from the bolt body. (Further disassembly is not required; doing so may result in your having to send the bolt back to be reassembled.)
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37
deepSteps.warn: Do not disassemble the striker assembly further. Knight says it may have to go back to the factory to be reassembled.

deepSteps.title: Striker back on, threaded to the end and no further
deepSteps.action: Thread the striker assembly clockwise into the bolt body and let it stop where it stops. No extra pressure at the end of the thread, and the striker is never tightened against the bolt housing — that pre-loads the assembly and changes how the striker sits.
deepSteps.caution: Do not tighten the striker against the bolt housing.
deepSteps.quote: 5.) To assemble, thread the striker assembly clockwise into the bolt body. Do not apply any pressure after the threading reaches the end. Do not tighten the striker against the bolt housing.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Index the reference points
deepSteps.action: Back the striker off anticlockwise until the reference points line up, thumb against the bolt to hold body and striker in register, then unscrew the secondary safety until its pressure is gone. If the marks do not line up, Knight has you repeat the sequence rather than force it — steps 2, 3, 5 and 6, in that order.
deepSteps.quote: 6.) When the striker assembly reaches the end of the threads, turn it counterclockwise, until reference points are aligned with each other. Hold your thumb against the bolt (this will help allow you to keep the bolt body striker assembly aligned correctly) then unscrew the secondary safety until there is no more pressure. If the assembly is not aligned, repeat steps 2, 3, 5, and 6.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Breech plug back in, greased
deepSteps.action: Grease the plug threads before it goes anywhere near the receiver — this is what stops the plug seizing next time. Run it in with the combo tool and hand tighten until it is firm against the back of the barrel and fully home. Hand tight is the specification; over-tightening is explicitly what makes it difficult to remove.
deepSteps.caution: Hand tight only. Do not over tighten the plug.
deepSteps.quote: 1.) Install the breech plug. Fill the threads of the plug with Knight® Breech Plug Grease™ to help prevent the breach plug sticking in the receiver. Using the breech plug end of the combo tool, insert the breech plug (I) into the rear of the receiver and hand tighten the plug into the receiver until it is firmly against the back of the barrel. Be sure the breech plug is screwed all the way into the receiver. Do not over tighten the plug or it will become difficult to remove.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — Disassembly and Assembly, Assembly — p.36

deepSteps.title: Bolt back in and safeties on
deepSteps.action: Hold the spring-loaded quick-release bolt screw out, slide the bolt fully home, release the screw, and put both safeties to safe before closing the handle. The rifle finishes this sequence cocked with both safeties on, which is the state it should be stored in.
deepSteps.quote: 7.) While pulling out on the spring-loaded Quick Release™ bolt screw (Photo #1), slide the bolt all the way back into the receiver. Release the bolt screw. Make sure the trigger and secondary safeties are both in the safe position. Close the bolt handle.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — DISC C-Toolless Bolt Removal and Disassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Optional: convert to bare 209 primers
deepSteps.action: The DISC Extreme is the one model in this group that Knight documents a conversion for. A different breech plug plus an adaptor in the bolt body lets it run bare 209 primers instead of the Full Plastic Jacket. Grease the new plug generously before it goes in, exactly as you would the original.
deepSteps.aside: This conversion is documented for the DISC Extreme only. Do not apply it to another model in this family.
deepSteps.quote: The DISC Extreme™ can be converted to use 209 primers with out the DISC Full Plastic Jacket™.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2025 EDITION — 2025 EDITION — 209 Conversion Non-Full Plastic Jacket Breech Plugs — p.37

cleaning.name: Barrel and breech
tasks: Scrub the bore breech-to-muzzle with a wet patch until patches come out clean
Scrub the breech plug threads in the receiver with a brush that reaches full depth
Clean the breech plug body and its flash channel
Dry the bore completely, then run an oiled patch through

cleaning.name: Bolt and receiver
tasks: Wash the breech plug and bolt in hot soapy water or Knight solvent
Pick the primer pocket / jacket seat in the bolt face clean of hardened residue
Brush the receiver interior and the bolt raceway
Dry every wetted surface, then oil with a water-displacing rust inhibitor

cleaning.name: Trigger group — solvent only
tasks: Clean the trigger assembly with solvent, never water
Do not leave the assembly soaking in solvent

cleaning.name: Stock and exterior
tasks: Wipe solvent and water off the stock before it soaks in
Check the recoil lug seat and stock screw hole are dry
Wipe all exterior metal with an oiled cloth

reassembly: Grease the breech plug threads and hand tighten the plug fully home — hand tight only.
Mount the trigger assembly with its screw and check it sits square against the receiver.
Hold the quick-release bolt screw open, slide the bolt fully in, then release it.
Put both the trigger safety and the secondary safety to safe before closing the bolt handle.
Set the barrelled action into the stock and tighten the single stock screw.
Return the ramrod to the stock.
fncheck: Before loading, clear the breech plug flash channel of cleaning oil: fit a primer, point the muzzle at the ground four to six inches from dirt or grass, and fire the primer. The dirt should visibly move — that is the channel proving clear. Repeat once, remove the spent primer, and return both safeties to safe. Then swab the bore with a wet patch and a dry patch, each contacting the breech plug, before the first charge.
